key_insight: An agentic workflow can automate the path from quantum protocol to neutral-atom QPU execution, but expert validation remains essential for scientific correctness.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the barrier to running quantum experiments on cloud-accessible neutral-atom hardware by streamlining design, compilation, simulation, and execution into a practical workflow.
method: Automated end-to-end pipeline for protocol-to-hardware translation on Pasqal neutral-atom QPUs
Kept the researcher in the loop for critical validation steps
Used a second agent to screen 633 Rydberg-array arXiv papers for hardware readiness
evidence_signal: In three case studies, the agent turned published work or patents into overnight QPU campaigns, and the paper reports that nearly half of 633 surveyed Rydberg-array papers appear implementable on current QPUs.
watch_item: The workflow can produce plausible but wrong choices or diagnoses, so expert review is still required before trusting experimental conclusions.
paper_title: Lowering the implementation barrier of neutral-atom quantum computing with agentic workflows
